knowledge_point.title: Identifying Equilibrium Solutions of a Differential Equation

question.:question/problem:
Consider the differential equation

$$
\frac{dy}{dt} = \frac{y^{2} - 1}{y^{2}}.
$$

Which of the following are equilibrium solutions? Select all that apply.
question.:question/worked-solution:
An equilibrium is a constant function $y(t)=c$. Set $dy/dt=0$ and test the resulting equation.

First keep the original domain: $y\ne0$.

We need

$$
f(c) = \frac{c^{2} - 1}{c^{2}}=0.
$$

- For $c=2$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(2) &=\frac{3}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=1$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1) &=0\end{aligned}
$$

This is zero, so it is an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=-1$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-1) &=0\end{aligned}
$$

This is zero, so it is an equilibrium solution.

Select $y=1$ and $y=-1$.

question.:question/problem:
Consider the differential equation

$$
\frac{dy}{dt} = - y^{2} - 3 y - 2.
$$

Which of the following are equilibrium solutions? Select all that apply.
question.:question/worked-solution:
An equilibrium is a constant function $y(t)=c$. Set $dy/dt=0$ and test the resulting equation.

We need

$$
f(c) = - c^{2} - 3 c - 2=0.
$$

- For $c=1$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1) &=-3 - 2 - 1 \\ &=-6\end{aligned}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=-1$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-1) &=-2 - 1 + 3 \\ &=0\end{aligned}
$$

This is zero, so it is an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=-2$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-2) &=-4 - 2 + 6 \\ &=0\end{aligned}
$$

This is zero, so it is an equilibrium solution.

Select $y=-1$ and $y=-2$.

knowledge_point.title: Identifying Equilibrium Solutions of a Differential Equation

question.:question/problem:
Consider the differential equation

$$
\frac{dy}{dt} = - y - \sin{\left(y \right)} - \pi.
$$

Which of the following are equilibrium solutions? Select all that apply.
question.:question/worked-solution:
An equilibrium is a constant function $y(t)=c$. Set $dy/dt=0$ and test the resulting equation.

We need

$$
f(c) = - c - \sin{\left(c \right)} - \pi=0.
$$

- For $c=0$: Use $\sin{\left(0 \right)}=0$.

$$
\begin{aligned}f(0) &=- \pi + 0 - \sin{\left(0 \right)} \\ &=- \pi\end{aligned}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=- \pi$: Use $\sin{\left(- \pi \right)}=0$.

$$
\begin{aligned}f(- \pi) &=- \pi - \sin{\left(- \pi \right)} + \pi \\ &=0\end{aligned}
$$

This is zero, so it is an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=\pi$: Use $\sin{\left(\pi \right)}=0$.

$$
\begin{aligned}f(\pi) &=- \pi - \pi - \sin{\left(\pi \right)} \\ &=- 2 \pi\end{aligned}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

Select $y=- \pi$.

question.:question/problem:
Consider the differential equation

$$
\frac{dy}{dt} = y^{2} \ln{\left(y \right)} - e^{2}.
$$

Which of the following are equilibrium solutions? Select all that apply.
question.:question/worked-solution:
An equilibrium is a constant function $y(t)=c$. Set $dy/dt=0$ and test the resulting equation.

First keep the original domain: $y>0$.

We need

$$
f(c) = c^{2} \ln{\left(c \right)} - e^{2}=0.
$$

- For $c=e$: Use $\ln{\left(e \right)}=1$.

$$
\begin{aligned}f(e) &=- e^{2} + e^{2} \ln{\left(e \right)} \\ &=0\end{aligned}
$$

This is zero, so it is an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=2$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(2) &=- e^{2} + 4 \ln{\left(2 \right)}\end{aligned}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=1$: Use $\ln{\left(1 \right)}=0$.

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1) &=- e^{2} + 1 \ln{\left(1 \right)} \\ &=- e^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

Select $y=e$.

question.:question/problem:
Consider the differential equation

$$
\frac{dy}{dt} + \frac{1}{\left(y + 1\right)^{2}} = 1.
$$

Which of the following are equilibrium solutions? Select all that apply.
question.:question/worked-solution:
An equilibrium is a constant function $y(t)=c$. Set $dy/dt=0$ and test the resulting equation.

First keep the original domain: $y + 1\ne0$.

Rearranging once, we need

$$
f(c) = 1 - \frac{1}{\left(c + 1\right)^{2}}=0.
$$

- For $c=2$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(2) &=- \frac{1}{9} + 1 \\ &=\frac{8}{9}\end{aligned}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=-2$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-2) &=-1 + 1 \\ &=0\end{aligned}
$$

This is zero, so it is an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=-3$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-3) &=- \frac{1}{4} + 1 \\ &=\frac{3}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

Select $y=-2$.

First keep the original domain: $y + 1>0$.

We need

$$
f(c) = \left(c + 1\right)^{2} \ln{\left(c + 1 \right)}=0.

$$

knowledge_point.title: Identifying Equilibrium Solutions of a Differential Equation

question.:question/problem:
Consider the differential equation

$$
\frac{dy}{dt} + \left(y + 1\right) = \left(y + 1\right) + \left(\left(y - 1\right)^{2} \ln{\left(y - 1 \right)} + e^{-2}\right).
$$

Which of the following are equilibrium solutions? Select all that apply.
question.:question/worked-solution:
An equilibrium is a constant function $y(t)=c$. Set $dy/dt=0$ and test the resulting equation.

First keep the original domain: $y - 1>0$.

Rearranging once, we need

$$
f(c) = \left(c - 1\right)^{2} \ln{\left(c - 1 \right)} + e^{-2}=0.
$$

- For $c=1 + e$: Use $\ln{\left(e \right)}=1$.

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1 + e) &=e^{-2} + e^{2} \ln{\left(e \right)} \\ &=e^{-2} + e^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=2$: Use $\ln{\left(1 \right)}=0$.

$$
\begin{aligned}f(2) &=1 \ln{\left(1 \right)} + e^{-2} \\ &=e^{-2}\end{aligned}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=e^{-1} + 1$: Use $\ln{\left(e^{-1} \right)}=-1$.

$$
\begin{aligned}f(e^{-1} + 1) &=\frac{\ln{\left(e^{-1} \right)}}{e^{2}} + e^{-2} \\ &=0\end{aligned}
$$

This is zero, so it is an equilibrium solution.

Select $y=e^{-1} + 1$.
